title: Knight+Rook VS Queen
reviewNotes: Reconstructed the initial six-piece board, full promotion-with-check mating line, Rf7 mate, and Rh7+/Rh1 defense. Three branches and every intermediate checked. h5+ is check and forces exactly three king replies; saved legal replay caught and removed an incorrect draft suggestion that immediate promotion was legal.
transcript: fools will resign. Whilst players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to win from this position. At first glance, it seems like white is just crushing, having a rook [music] and a knight. But then we realize that black is only one step away from getting a new queen, and that there is no way to prevent the promotion. If the rook comes down, the pawn can just take it. So, white has to become creative and find the precise and brilliant pawn to h5, sacrificing the pawn and giving the black king only three possible moves. First of all, if the king goes to f6, this is very simple because rook to f7 is a surprising checkmate. And if the king takes the pawn, now after rook h7 check, we are able to come to h1 and stop the promotion from in front of it. So, black's best try after h5 is to play king to h6. But now we can give a check with the knight and insist that the king takes the pawn, because if he doesn't, after a series of precise checks, we are going to [music] build a mating net around the king. Again, you cannot take here because the rook is going to come to the first rank. But after king to g6, now king g4 seals the deal. You cannot stop rook to e6, even if you promote with a queen. Rook e6 check is almost checkmate, which forces black to sacrifice the queen and white would win the game. But okay, so what? Black is not naive enough to enter that line. And instead, after the check from the knight, he's just going to take the pawn because of course now the rook cannot give a check anymore. But what white can do is give another check. And again, black has a choice, either to come back up or to go further down. If the king comes up, we give another check and we're either going to fork the king and the first [music] rank, or if the king takes the knight, now we can give another check here and this time after we move the king, we are stopping the promotion and we're going to checkmate with the rook. But okay, again, black can just avoid that and decide instead to keep going down with the king. And now finally, it seems like black is simply out of the woods. There is no way to attack this king safely. So, is this it? Is black simply out of the woods? Well, not exactly. White has the majestic and brilliant knight to G5. This allows black to promote with a check, but this time we can cover that check with our own check on the black [music] king. King H3. After rook H5 and king to G2, it is black's queen to support the final blow in this game. Because rook to H2 is a beautiful checkmate.
